subject: Strategic bid match and transition playbook for Pegasus
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@pegasusht.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Thompson <mthompson@pegasusht.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Rivulet counteroffer — can Redwood match?

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the private deployment options. We’ve been running a parallel procurement process and Rivulet came back with a fairly aggressive commercial: 30% off list for year one, onboarding credits equivalent to ~$120k, and a 3-month free pilot.

Pegasus is interested in Redwood because of the unified runtime and the KV caching capabilities, but given budget constraints we need to understand what you can do on price and transition economics. Specifically:
- Can Redwood match or exceed the onboarding credit?
- Any flexibility on list discounts for year one vs multi-year?
- Will you cover data migration assistance for our on-prem private deployment?

We’ve attached the Rivulet proposal for context. Our procurement lead (cc’d) will want a clear comparison and an expected migration playbook if we decide to move.

[Attachment: Rivulet_proposal.pdf (1.2MB)]

Looking for a response before EOD Friday so we can decide whether to proceed to commercial redlines.

Best,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
VP, Platform Engineering
Pegasus HealthTech

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@pegasusht.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rivulet counteroffer — can Redwood match?

Alicia — thanks for the clarity and for sharing Rivulet’s terms. Quick responses up front: we can be competitive on credits and we have a structured migration playbook for private deployments.

Before we put a formal offer on the table, two asks:
1) Can you share 12-month projected token consumption (avg QPS, tail-latency SLA needs, and embedding volume)?
2) Any firm contract must include your procurement timeline and required PO terms (term length, renewal language, data retention SLAs).

High-level proposal (subject to usage and legal):
- Up to 18% off list for the first 12 months (with stepped pricing options for 24/36 month commits)
- $150k migration credit applied as a one-time invoice credit to offset onboarding and engineering hours
- 3 months of reduced-rate pilot (50% off host fees) with a formal mutual action plan to ensure cutover windows
- Dedicated onboarding engineer for the first 90 days for the private deployment; optional add-on for on-prem workstation access for data transfer needs

I’m looping in Laura and Tessa to help with the formal commercial and to validate we can scope the migration credit appropriately. I’ll put together a short playbook draft and a sample term sheet.

Chuck in the specifics and we’ll run it past Legal. Sound reasonable?

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@pegasusht.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Thompson <mthompson@pegasusht.com>, procurement@pegasusht.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Rivulet counteroffer — can Redwood match?

Hi Priyom — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached are the usage tables and our procurement checklist. Highlights:
- Expected steady-state: ~12B tokens/month, peak bursts to 30B tokens for training/retrospective analysis windows
- Embedding volume: ~1.5M vectors/month
- Mandatory: SOC2 type II evidence, audited data-retention controls, proof of on-prem install window with minimal downtime

On the competitive side, Rivulet is offering a one-time professional services credit ($120k) and 3 months free of service on the hosted side. They also committed to a migration SLA that guarantees a 6-week cutover with payback for missed milestones.

We like Redwood’s architecture but need the economics to line up. If you can firm up the playbook and include an explicit milestone-based credit release, that will help. We can be flexible on contract length if the first-year unit economics are strong.

Thanks,
Alicia

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@pegasusht.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, procurement@pegasusht.com
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood commercial proposal — PG-7893 (term sheet attached)

Alicia / Procurement team — following up with a formal commercial position from Redwood based on the usage tables you provided. We appreciate the competitive context. Below is our offer and the trigger conditions for credit release.

Commercial summary (high level):
- Year 1 list discount: 18% off standard hosted/private pricing
- Migration credit: $150,000 applied as an invoice credit upon execution of SOW and first milestone (environment provisioning + KV cache validation)
- Pilot: 3-month pilot at 50% of list (or, alternatively, 1 month fully free + 2 months at 60%) — your choice
- Support: included 24/7 incident response for first 12 months and a dedicated onboarding engineer for the first 90 days
- SLAs: 99.5% uptime for the dedicated private cluster; penalties for missed availability milestones per term sheet

Milestone-based credit release:
1) 30% of credit on signed SOW + environment provisioning
2) 40% on data migration completion and KV cache validation
3) 30% on successful production cutover within the agreed window

We’ve attached a redlineable term sheet (PDF). Key legal points that we’re open to negotiating: renewal notice window, data retention language, and liability caps tied to committed spend. We’re unable to match an up-front 30% list discount, but believe the migration economics and bundled support create superior total cost of ownership during the first 12–18 months.

Next steps:
- If this aligns, procurement to provide a PO template and preferred contract redline window (we typically require 5 business days for initial review)
- We can host a technical cutover runbook session next week with our infra team to walk through the migration plan

[Attachment: term-sheet-PG-7893.pdf (220KB)]

Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@pegasusht.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Thompson <mthompson@pegasusht.com>, procurement@pegasusht.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood commercial proposal — PG-7893 (term sheet attached)

Laura — thank you for the clear proposal and the milestone schedule. This is the most concrete offer we’ve seen so far and the milestone-based credit release is preferable to a lump-sum. A couple of ask items before I confirm:
- Can we extend the pilot choice to 4 weeks fully free + 2 months at 60%? The longer free window helps our clinical QA team clear the validation gate.
- Please add language that Redwood will provide a named escalation contact during the pilot for SLA exceptions.
- Procurement will prepare a PO and will need a redline period of 7 business days for the term sheet (we will push for a 5-day turnaround but want the option).

If you can accept the pilot tweak and the named escalation commitment, I’m prepared to move this to commercial redlines and schedule a kick-off for the week of 31 May. We’ll send the PO template to procurement@redwood.ai and loop in our legal for the term sheet.

Thanks — Alicia
